test_title: PYST 16: SSC CGL 2025 - General Knowledge (Held On: 17th_September_2025_Shift_1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following pairs (Educational Event - Key Outcome/Initiative) is correctly matched?

options.text: Charter Act, 1813 – Allocated funds for promotion of education
Macaulay's Minute, 1835 – Emphasized traditional Sanskrit learning
Serampore Mission – Promoted technical education for elite Indians
Orientalist-Anglicist Debate – Resolved by Charter Act, 1833

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: Charter Act, 1813 – Allocated funds for promotion of education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Charter Act of 1813 was a landmark legislation that marked the beginning of formal state support for education in India.
 
• It allocated a sum of Rs. 1 lakh annually for the promotion of education among Indians. This was the first instance of the British government funding education in India.
 
• The Act emphasized the need for promoting knowledge of sciences and literature in India, focusing on Western education.
 
• This initiative laid the foundation for future educational reforms and the establishment of institutions to impart Western-style education.
 
• The Charter Act, 1813, also allowed missionaries to spread education and Christianity in India, further influencing the educational landscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evolution of Education Policies in Colonial India**

 
 
• The question revolves around key milestones in the history of education during British rule in India.
 
• Various policies, acts, and initiatives shaped the educational system, transitioning from traditional Indian learning to Western-style education.
 
• Important events like the Charter Act, Macaulay's Minute, and contributions of missionaries played vital roles in transforming education in colonial India.
